questions.knowledge_point: Calculating an Element of the Inverse of a 3x3 Matrix
questions.problem: Determine the entry ${a}_{12}^{′}$ in the inverse of a matrix $A$ $=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ if its determinant is $-2.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we want the entry ${a}_{12}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{21}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{21} & =(-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(3-0) \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{12}^{′}=\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{21}=\frac{1}{-2}\cdot (-3)=\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating an Element of the Inverse of a 3x3 Matrix
questions.problem: Determine the entry ${a}_{31}^{′}$ in the inverse of a matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the determinant of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(A)=|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| & =0|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|-0|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =0-0+(0-2) \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{31}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{13}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{13} & =(-1)^{1+3}|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =0-2 \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{31}^{′}=\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{13}=\frac{1}{-2}\cdot (-2)=1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Cofactor Method To Solve for an Unknown Quantity
questions.problem:
The entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & k \\ -1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]$
equals $-1$ and $det(A)=4-2k.$ Find the value of $k.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, note that we are given the determinant of $A:$

$$
det(A)=4-2k
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{23}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{23} & =(-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(2-0) \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{32}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{23} \\  & =\frac{1}{4-2k}\cdot (-2) \\  & =\frac{1}{k-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{32}^{′}=-1$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{k-2} & =-1 \\ 1 & =2-k \\ k & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The entry ${a}_{13}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & k & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]$
equals $-\frac{1}{2}$ and $det(A)=k-2.$ Find the value of $k.$

$k=${{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
First, note that we are given the determinant of $A:$

$$
det(A)=k-2
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{13}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{13}^{t}={c}_{31}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{31} & =(-1)^{3+1}|\begin{aligned}k & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}k & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =k+2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{13}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{13}^{t} \\  & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{31} \\  & =\frac{1}{(k-2)}\cdot (k+2) \\  & =\frac{k+2}{\,k-2\,}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{13}^{′}=-\frac{1}{2}$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{k+2}{\,k-2\,} & =-\frac{1}{2} \\ 2(k+2) & =-(k-2) \\ 2k+4 & =-k+2 \\ 3k & =-2 \\ k & =-\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The entry ${a}_{23}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 3 & k & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

equals $-1.$ Find the value of $k.$

$k=${{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the determinant of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 3 & k & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ k & -2\end{aligned}|-(-1)|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & k\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(1\cdot (-2)-(-1)\cdot k)+(0\cdot (-2)-(-1)\cdot 3)+(0\cdot k-1\cdot 3) \\  & =2(k-2)+3-3 \\  & =2k-4\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{23}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{23}^{t}={c}_{32}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{32} & =(-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(2\cdot (-1)-1\cdot 0) \\  & =-(-2) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{23}^{′} & =\frac{1}{det(A)}{c}_{23}^{t} \\  & =\frac{1}{det(A)}{c}_{32} \\  & =\frac{2}{2k-4} \\  & =\frac{1}{k-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{23}^{′}=-1$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{k-2} & =-1 \\ 1 & =-(k-2) \\ k-2 & =-1 \\ k & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
